defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: Dedup removes new_m before confirming old_m exists; if old_m isn't found, ValueError is raised and new_m is lost from the scene
Dedup only handles the same list/parent-child, not sibling groups; new_m can end up duplicated across groups
votes.evidence_quote: The guard removes `new_m` before confirming `old_m` exists in the tree. If `old_m` is not found, `ValueError` is raised but `new_m` has already been silently removed from the scene.
votes.justification: The review points at the right code and the right mechanism: the dedup removes an object before the search, which causes a ValueError and partial state. But it describes the case where old_m is absent, not the case where new_m is old_m. It never notes that scene.replace(a, a) breaks because the dedup removes the very object being searched for.
